heroAnswer: Troy was built on the river. The river built the town, flooded the town, and now the town is built against it. We serve Troy with free inspections, transparent pricing, and photo-documented work.
intro: Troy is our service area's first county seat — platted in 1807 to be the seat of justice, drowned in 1913, rebuilt behind levees, and still the county seat. Its housing is old-leaning: 60.6% built before 1980, the 1960s cohort the largest single decade, and a pre-war core of 15.7%. The discovery moment is a 1960s ranch whose original plumbing finally lets go, or a pre-war basement damp for decades — plus two city tornadoes (2020 EF0, 2022 EF1) whose roof valleys can leak for seasons.

moldNote: Troy's mold risk is age plus river plus storms: 60.6% pre-1980 housing, river-valley water table near Morgan Ditch, and tornado roof damage in 2020 and 2022. No current flood claim is made — the 1913 flood is history, the levee system its sequel.
